title: CLI errors print to stdout instead of stderr, defeating shell 2>/dev/null guards

description:
WHAT: Every error from the main CLI dispatch path is written to stdout via print!, not stderr. Confirmed empirically: `story move SH-41 done x --quiet >out 2>err` yields 54 bytes on stdout and 0 bytes on stderr (exit 2).

WHERE: src/main.rs lines 28, 68, and 81 all call print!("{}", output::render_error(...)). Only the TUI path (main.rs:13,17) and the web --serve path (main.rs:44,49) correctly use eprintln!.

WHEN / LAST KNOWN GOOD: none — present since aee7bac (2026-03-11, 'feat: add core story cli workflow'). This is a day-one defect, not a regression.

EXTENT (why it matters):
1. Callers cannot suppress errors with 2>/dev/null. The storyhook-managed post-merge hook does exactly this: `story move $ID done ... --quiet 2>/dev/null || true`. Because the error lands on stdout, it leaks into unrelated output — observed during a routine fast-forward of main, which printed 'error: story SH-41 is closed and cannot be modified' in the middle of the merge diffstat.
2. With --json, error payloads are interleaved into the stdout data stream that scripts parse as results.
3. Violates the POSIX convention that diagnostics go to stderr and results to stdout, which every piping/scripting consumer assumes.

REPRO:
  story move <any-closed-id> done "probe" --quiet >/tmp/out 2>/tmp/err; echo "exit=$?"
  wc -c </tmp/out   # 54 — should be 0
  wc -c </tmp/err   # 0  — should be 54

FIX SKETCH: change the three print! calls to eprint! . Note render_error already returns a trailing newline, so eprint! (not eprintln!) preserves current formatting.

REGRESSION TEST: assert an erroring invocation writes an empty stdout and a non-empty stderr, for both plain and --json modes.

text: [git] b60db32: chore(storyhook): file SH-59 and SH-60, two defects found reconciling main

Fixed in commit da3109d (branch rearch/w0-gate-repair, W0.1). All three dispatch paths (parse failure, cwd resolution, command failure) now go through one fail() helper in main.rs. Ruling on the --json contract, as asked: the envelope STAYS on stdout and only plain-text diagnostics move. With --json, stdout is a machine-readable result channel carrying exactly one self-describing document per run ({result: ok|conflict|error, exit_code: N}), and the error envelope is the result the caller asked for. Existing tests state this deliberately, not incidentally - move_if_state.rs reads a result:conflict envelope off stdout for an exit-2 invocation, and plugin/claude-code/bin/story.sh's CAS claim depends on that same envelope captured from stdout with 2>/dev/null. Splitting it to stderr would force every consumer to read two streams to find one answer, on a stream that also carries free-text hook warnings (event_hooks.rs) that would break jq outright. test-dispatch-claim-conflict.sh is the empirical check on that ruling and passes unchanged. Regression tests in tests/cli_error_streams.rs: failed command writes to stderr and nothing to stdout with its exit code intact; --quiet does not put it back (the reported post-merge-hook symptom); parser usage errors behave the same; a successful command stays silent on stderr; --json still emits one parseable envelope on stdout with stderr empty. Red 3 of 5, green after. 73 existing assertions across 18 test files were characterizing the bug and now assert stderr; no message text changed. Not covered: the cwd-resolution path, which needs a process started in a directory that no longer exists - the harness sets the child's cwd, so it cannot arrange that. cargo test 48 targets green, plugin suite 15/15.
